sentences: On behalf of the senator, the owner of the world's largest Chinese jade collection, detective the policeman investigate a death threat involving the priceless jade tablets that were brought to the country by three adventurers, who are now on the hit list of an oriental gang.
A note written in Chinese warns the impending doom at midnight unless a ransom is paid for the valuable jades, which have been stolen.
The policeman is put on the case to protect the people who were involved in smuggling the jades into the country.

That night, the reporter joins the policeman at the club where he and his assistant the assistant are guarding the threatened victims, the first adventurer, the second adventurer and the third adventurer.
Once midnight has passed, they leave, but the first adventurer is machine-gunned in his car and killed.
A note found in the car warns that the second adventurer will be the next to die.
He is later found dead after smoking a poisoned cigarette, and his body vanishes mysteriously before the coroner arrives at the crime scene.
The senator's daughter the young woman and her fiancé the young man, are ordered by the mysterious killer to deliver $250,000 ransom to the last buoy in the nearby city harbor.
The reporter discovered that the first adventurer's fingerprints and those of the body in the morgue do not match.
She joins the policeman in a navy submarine as the young man rides out to pay the ransom.

At the appointed place, the reporter and the policeman surface in the submarine, just in time to save the young man and prove that the murders were all part of an elaborate plot by the first adventurer, the second adventurer, and the third adventurer to extort money from the senator.
The reporter is covering a bank robbery, one of a series committed by the bank robber.
Returning to her newspaper, the reporter is stopped by a policeman for speeding.
Because she doesn't have her driver's license with her, he takes her to court.
While in court, the reporter encounters the shoplifter, who is the girlfriend of notorious bank robber the bank robber and is sentenced to jail for shoplifting.
After the reporter's boyfriend, the lieutenant, identifies her, the reporter is released.
However, the reporter asks the lieutenant to put her back in jail after realizing that the shoplifter is the bank robber's girlfriend.
The reporter gets herself thrown into jail so that she can befriend the shoplifter and use her to get a lead on the bank robber.
The reporter has no luck with her plan until she helps subdue another prisoner who tries to stab the shoplifter.
The shoplifter suggests that she and the reporter escape from jail.
The lieutenant agrees to cooperate with the reporter's plan when she explains that the reward money for the bank robber's capture will enable them to get married.
With the help and collusion of the lieutenant and the police, she escapes with the shoplifter to the coastal city, where the shoplifter is meeting her boyfriend.
The two escapees are followed by the lieutenant and his assistant, the assistant.
The lieutenant hopes to capture the bank robber to collect the $5,000 reward as a down payment for a house for him and the reporter.
He decides not to notify the local police of the bank robber's expected arrival, but his actions are so suspicious that the police think he and the assistant are criminals.
The local policeman, a coastal city policeman, follows them, but the lieutenant succeeds in convincing him that the assistant is a wrestler and that he is his manager.
Meanwhile, the reporter has arranged to signal the lieutenant when the bank robber arrives by hanging her stockings on the fire escape.
The assistant sees the shoplifter hang her stockings out to dry and they burst into the room, only to find that the bank robber has not arrived yet.
The reporter quickly makes up a story to explain their presence.
When the bank robber finally arrives, one of his men recognizes the lieutenant as a policeman but pretends that the lieutenant is another criminal.
The lieutenant, not knowing that they recognize him, invites the bank robber to join him in robbing the wrestling stadium.
The bank robber agrees to the plan but arranges for his men to kidnap the lieutenant on the way there.
At the wrestling arena, another reporter recognizes the reporter and reveals her identity.

After getting rid of the bank robber's men, the lieutenant rushes to the arena where the assistant, posing as a wrestler named the stage name, gets thrown out of the ring just in time to land on the bank robber, who is trying to escape.
The lieutenant and the assistant are credited with the arrest, and the reporter and the lieutenant now have the money to marry.
The reporter writes a series of articles criticizing the mayor the politician, accusing him of colluding with local crime boss the crime boss and the crime boss's illegal activities.
The reporter is getting all her information straight from the mayor's office, using a listening device.
The reporter's boyfriend, detective the policeman is concerned about the articles, believing that they are placing her in danger.
The crime boss asks his allies to withdraw advertising from the reporter's newspaper and pressure her editor into canceling her articles.
The reporter is determined to prove that her articles are correct.
She overhears the crime boss telling the mayor about his "little red book" with all of his transactions and illegal payoffs and finds the book after breaking into the crime boss's house.
The crime boss reports the burglary to police and demands the return of his book.
The reporter writes more articles exposing the crime boss, but her story is rejected by her newspaper editor, fearing more syndicates will pull advertising from the paper.
She goes to all other newspapers, who all refused to print the story, then she encounters the newspaperman the publisher of a small and relatively unknown newspaper.
The newspaperman decides to print the story and the reporter distributes the publication around the city with the help of the police driver.

After the reporter revealed the mayor's corruption, the resultant publicity forces a recall election with the citizens choosing the newspaperman as the new candidate running against the corrupt mayor.
However, during the election, the newspaperman is murdered by the crime boss with a fatal injection.
The policeman, who is annoyed at the reporter's interference, writes her name as the new candidate as a joke.
To his dismay, the reporter decides to run for mayor seriously and is winning voters.
The crime boss's man kidnaps the reporter and drugs her.
The policeman threatens the crime boss to no avail but found an address where he believes the crime boss is keeping the reporter.
The policeman and the police driver track down the house and fight the crime boss and his men and save the reporter.
A half dozen policeman arrived at the house arresting them.
The crime boss manages to escape in the police driver's police car but is killed when the car explodes.
The reporter wins the election but decides, when presented with a baby to hold for a photograph, that she doesn't want to be the mayor and wants to marry the policeman instead.
The detective's testimony results in a death sentence for convicted murderer the convict (the actor playing the convict).
However, he escapes and heads to a wax museum, a secret Mob hideout run by the surgeon (the actor.
The surgeon, a crooked "facial surgeon", operates on the convict, changing his appearance.
The detective is lured to the wax museum on the pretext of sparring over an old case with the criminologist (the actor playing the criminologist) on a radio broadcast arranged by the surgeon.
Based on the criminologist's testimony, the executed man had been to be executed, but the detective is convinced that the executed man was innocent.
In fact, it is all a setup so that the convict can have his revenge, but the detective already suspects it.
His son the youth (the actor playing the youth) sneaks into the museum to investigate (without the detective's knowledge).
When everyone gathers at the museum, the lawyer barges in, representing the executed man's widow.
His client also sneaks in.
When the principals gather around a table to reenact a scene from the executed man's case for the broadcast, the surgeon makes sure the detective is in the seat wired for an electrocution.
However, the criminologist insists on changing seats.
Museum night watchman the watchman is tricked into throwing the switch.
The lights go out, and the criminologist dies... but not from electricity.
(The assistant, the surgeon's assistant, had cut the wire in an attempt to keep the museum's other function a secret.)
The detective finds a small puncture wound in the dead man's neck and a bamboo blowgun dart.
The detective becomes certain that the gangster framed the executed man, his business partner, and that he killed the criminologist as well.
The gangster was supposedly murdered by the convict, another business partner and a friend of the executed man's.
With the surgeon having operated on the gangster, no one knows who among those gathered at the museum is him (the youth even suspects the executed man's widow).
The gangster kills the convict and makes an attempt on the detective's life, before the detective finally unmasks and captures him.
The detective must stop a spy from destroying the canal, trapping a Navy fleet on its way to the western ocean after maneuvers in the eastern ocean.
As the country's fleet prepares to navigate the waters of the canal, the nearby city becomes rife with spies.
A new group of suspects appears with the arrival of a sea plane bound for the port town.

Among the suspects are novelist the writer, matronly school teacher the teacher, sinister scientist the researcher, café proprietor the café owner, singer the singer (real name the singer's true name), cigarette salesman the salesman, government engineer the engineer and government agent the agent.
Upon landing, the agent goes to a hat shop owned by the hatter, alias the detective, to enlist the sleuth's help in unmasking the deadly spy known only as the saboteur.
Just as the agent is about to divulge the saboteur's real identity, he falls to the ground, dead, leaving the detective to expose the saboteur before the spy can sabotage the canal.
The agent died from a poison-laced cigarette that could only have been planted on him by a fellow seaplane passenger, so the detective keeps a weather eye on them during their hotel holdover.
Number two Son the youth is not only arrested for taking pictures, he spills the beans about his father's actual identity.
He is discovered hiding under the bed in the writer's hotel room, looking for clues.
A search of the room is forestalled by the singer's arrival.
She begs the detective not to give away her "without passport" status.
She had to flee when the invaders took over her homeland.
After she leaves, the youth throws a porcelain tobacco container at a gun hand peeking through the door.
The broken container holds a detailed map of a nearby cemetery.
This discovery prompts a further search of the room, where the writer's corpse is found in the closet, fatally shot.
It develops he was undercover for the British intelligence service.
The map leads to the café owner's family tomb, which the detective discovers had been outfitted as a modern spy hideout.
The teacher blunders onto the scene, and then somebody locks them in the tomb.
Disguised as a water delivery man, a henchman has delivered a "water cooler" of nitro to the main power plant building.
The henchman makes the mistake of returning to the tomb, unwittingly releasing the detective and the youth and the captain.
During a graveyard chase, the henchman is shot dead and is revealed to be the café owner.
None of the "good guys" fired their guns, so who killed him?
The detective learns that the canal's key locks are to be blown up at ten that night.
The detective then sequesters the suspects at the plant, forcing the teacher to expose herself as the saboteur in order to escape death.
With the saboteur under arrest, the fleet sails safely through the locks to protect democracy.
The detective then reveals he had previously defused her explosive device.
The famed detective seeks to unmask a killer on a voyage across the ocean.
It begins harmlessly enough, with the detective catching No.2 and No.7 Sons in his office;trying to destroy a bad report card from school.
They are ordered to leave when retired police force man the inspector arrives—they leave, but they eavesdrop.
The inspector is certain there is a mass killer aboard a cruise ship that is now docked in the island port.
A big city judge was strangled in his stateroom, and he asks the detective to join the cruise and investigate.
The detective leaves briefly to get permission from his superiors---and the strangler leans in an open window and kills the inspector.
While absent, the detective learned there had been ANOTHER murder at the hotel where the cruise passengers are staying.
Finding his dead friend, he vows to pursue the case until the end.

Aboard ship, the detective has only a day and a half before the ship docks in the mainland port and the passengers will all scatter to their homes.The detective's son is quickly discovered hiding in a lifeboat---the detective allows him to be thrown in the brig, sensing the detective's son will be sentenced to work his way through, he is—as a steward with free rein of the staterooms.This was the detective's intent.
Cruise director the doctor seems overly eager to keep the murders from becoming public knowledge.
We have dizzy matron the wealthy woman;her patient secretary the young woman;and the wealthy woman's jovial traveling companion the fellow traveller.
The professor bills himself as a traveling archeologist.

The spiritualist pair are an eerily deadpan couple who spend half their time in the "spirit world"And the nervous passenger is a nervous wreck who confines himself to his stateroom(assuming he hasn't been sneaking out).

The detective finally gets it out of the nervous passenger that his wife's first husband swore revenge on them for sending him to prison(he was guilty), and the dead Judge had been the one who sentenced him.
The guard, a tough sailor, guards the nervous passenger's door---but one night he is decoyed away and knocked out---and the nervous passenger is killed and 30 pieces of Silver left by the body.
A muted fun-and-games party has been taking place upstairs, with many candid photos taken.The detective collects all the negatives, hoping to see who was unaccounted for at the time of the murder.
But the killer(disguised in beard and mask) knocks the detective out and takes the negatives.
During a below decks chase, the thief is shot and killed.
But the negatives aren't on him.It is revealed to be the fellow traveller.
But the detective says it isn't over—the fellow traveller was a mere accomplice who would don the disguise as a decoy.
The actual killer was blackmailing him;the fellow traveller was secretly a jewelry fence who had done business with the killer in the past.
The nervous passenger's wife, the REAL target all along, is brought to the mainland port docks; apparently crippled and blinded from an auto accident.
But her mere presence goads the killer into making a fatal mistake, and justice is done at last.
They still must convince the detective's son, who is nervously holding the doctor at gunpoint.
The professor, a God-fearing physical culturist, arrives to work in the serene little town.
He claims to be a specialist and top authority on health matters.
The town physician, the doctor, reacts to the professor's promises to the women in town of dramatic weight loss, if they followed his advice.
The head of the town women's club, the matron, is charmed by the questionable professor.
The professor and invites him to her home and to have a lecture when the club is meeting.
He is welcome to use the club as his forum for his teachings.
The professor starts teaching the women about strict diet being the best road to self-satisfaction.

The doctor, on the other hand, begins to warn the women about the dangers with wholesale diets, claiming that all diets should be tailored to fit the individual and advising the women not to listen to the professor.
The professor's teachings result in the disruption of the town women's eating routines.
They also disrupt the peace and quiet in the matron's family life, causing the matron and her husband to argue about the professor's teachings and intrusions on the town life.
The matron's daughter, the girl, has taken an interest in the professor's assistant, the young man, and started an extreme diet to seem more pleasing to him.
The girl soon collapses from starvation.
The doctor claims the professor is a fraud and a charlatan.
The town doesn't listen to his warnings.
The girl's condition gets worse and the doctor, exhausted from an abnormal workload because of the professor's teachings, manages to visit her.
While examining her he discovers that the professor has given the girl, and the other women, benzedrine.
The doctor finally discloses the professor and his cultist teachings as a public hazard.
The heresies of the professor come to the young man's knowledge, and he finally realizes that his boss is a fraud.
He quits and runs to the girl's bedside.
With the help of a blood transfusion he manages to save the girl's life.
The town women are taken off their unhealthy diets and life in town returns to normal, after the professor is driven off, disclosed as a quack.
Later, the young man and the girl are married.
On the last day of the school year, the plain 25-year-old young teacher has her student, the boy, write punishment lines on the blackboard.
After the class is dismissed, she releases the boy and tells him that few can do what they want in life, so they might as well make the best of what they have.
She is overheard by the colleague, an older teacher.
The colleague tells the young teacher that she regrets not doing wild things when she was young.
She advises the young teacher to do what she never did and the young teacher decides to take her advice for one day.
She buys a pretty dress and hosiery and releases her pet canary.
Sitting in a public park, the young teacher is propositioned by the flirt, a persistent guy who will not go away.
The young teacher finally knocks him down and drives off in his car.
The flirt turns out to be a killer, he stole the car she is in and on the floor of the back seat is a body, that he and his partner, have murdered.
The gang leader, their boss, is displeased when he learns that the body is hidden under his overcoat, which has a label with his name on it.
The gang leader gives the partner ten hours to get the coat back, or else.
The police are also looking for the stolen vehicle.
Unaware of any of this, the young teacher picks up a stranded man, whose car has broken down.
The police officer spots the car and gives chase, but the young teacher manages to lose him.
They head to the local country club for refreshments.
The stranded man turns out to know far more about the young teacher's predicament than she does, pointing out that she has a corpse in the back seat.
The informer, a snitch, runs into the partner and tells him he found the car he is looking for.
After the partner leaves, the informer telephones the police officer.
When the stranded man sees the police officer by the car, he points the partner out as the driver.
While the police officer is chasing the partner, the stranded man and the young teacher drive away.
They stop for gas at a station.
The attendant recognizes them as fugitives, but the stranded man ties him up.
A rich elderly woman, the dowager, pulls up in her chauffeur-driven limousine and while they are distracted, the stranded man switches license plates.
Then the stranded man and the young teacher break into an empty house, but the partner and the flirt track them down.
Fortunately, the stranded man manages to knock the partner out and the flirt runs away after the young teacher burns him with a cigarette.
The dowager also shows up, after an encounter with the police officer.
It comes out that they "broke into" the stranded man's home; the car is also the stranded man's.
Despite the young teacher's assumption, he is not a crook.
When the pair return the car to the park for the police to find, two other gang members take them at gunpoint to the gang leader.
Then the dowager bursts in.
She was following in her car and, when she saw her friends being captured, sent her chauffeur for the police, who arrive and capture the gang.
Afterward, the young teacher tells her grandmother that she and the stranded man are getting married.
Her grandmother tells her that her canary has returned too, also with a companion.
At the family mansion, the heir gives his fiancée a very valuable diamond necklace, a family heirloom.
The informant telephones the crook to let him know that the couple have just left with the necklace.
The blackmailer, the husband the fiancée thought was dead, would rather blackmail his wife, but the crook wants the necklace.
The blackmailer confronts the fiancée and forcibly takes the necklace, but is shot and killed by an unseen murderer, who takes the jewelry.
Panicking, the fiancée flees her apartment.
Waiting outside, the crook is puzzled.
The speeding valet nearly runs the fiancée down.
A motorcycle policeman arrests her, the valet and his employer, the adventurer, the happily retired gentleman criminal with a famous nickname.
However, the fiancée blurts out that she is involved in a murder, so the adventurer gives the policeman the slip.
He takes the fiancée back to her apartment, examines it and the body for clues, and provides her with a cover story.
As the adventurer and the valet are leaving, they are spotted and overheard by the crook.
When the police arrive, the inspector believes the fiancée, until he learns that the door was not forced and a key found on the dead man fits the lock.
He decides to take her in for further questioning, but lets her get properly dressed first.
She escapes, as the inspector had hoped, as he has arranged to have her followed.
She finds the adventurer's address in the telephone directory and heads there.
The crook gets there first, convinced that the adventurer and the fiancée are working together to steal the necklace.
Then the fiancée arrives.
After the valet takes the crook into the next room at gunpoint, the adventurer learns about the incriminating key and that the fiancée got away so easily.
When the inspector shows up, as the adventurer had expected, the adventurer hides the fiancée in a secret compartment.
After the police and the crook leave, the adventurer and the fiancée go to see the dealer, a fence the adventurer knows, to ask him to find out if anybody is trying to sell the necklace.
The crook comes to the adventurer's place while he is out, but the fiancée is present.
He then recognizes the person who fled the apartment where the blackmailer was killed from a newspaper photo of the people who were present when the fiancée received the necklace.
After locking the fiancée and the valet up, he telephones the person and demands the necklace be brought to his place in 15 minutes.
The valet has, however, turned on a recording device.
The heir and the adventurer arrive just after the crook leaves.
The adventurer receives a call from the dealer, who informs him the necklace had been broken up and sold piecemeal a year before.
The recording proves helpful, and the adventurer and the heir race away.
They get the blackmailer's address from his dry cleaner, who then calls the inspector.
They find the crook dead.
From a clue, the adventurer thinks he has solved the case, but the inspector and his men arrive and arrest him.
Fortunately for the adventurer, the heir produces a gun.
The adventurer telephones the fiancée and has her inform the suspects that he has figured out who the murderer is and the location of the necklace, in the river beside the fiancée's apartment.
While the heir holds the others prisoner, the adventurer takes the inspector to the fiancée's place.
First the family friend, then another guest, and finally the heir's mother drive up.
The adventurer eventually identifies the family friend as the killer.
On a flight to the city for an annual police convention, the detective encounters his old police force friend, the agent (an actor).
The agent is now a member of military intelligence trying to track down what he believes is a sabotage ring led by a ringleader.
A bomber and its pilots crashed the day before.
The detective offers his assistance.
The detective is welcomed at the airport by the inspector from the city police and, to the detective's surprise, his number two son.
The detective goes to see the agent the next day at the apartment of the executive, where a dinner party is in progress.
He finds his friend dead of poison gas in the executive's library, where he had gone to do some work.
The agent's briefcase, containing all the information he had gathered about the sabotage ring, is missing.
The window is latched, so the detective concludes one of the guests is responsible.
The detective discovers that the agent asked that his university classmate, the actress and the designer, chief designer at the aircraft company, be invited to the party.
The executive himself is the company president.
The lost bomber crashed at the company's plant.
Also present is the stockbroker.
A servant reports the chemist insisted on seeing the agent, so he showed him in.
The detective learns that the actress also spoke with the agent that night, on behalf of a friend, the young woman.
The young woman, it turns out, married the ringleader in a far-off country.
When she found out the ringleader was involved in sabotage, she fled, only to be pursued by her husband and his assistant, the henchman.
The henchman is eventually tracked down, with the young woman's help, and taken into custody.
(During a police lineup of Indians, a petty crook, aka a nickname, is revealed to be a faker, not a fakir.
Before the henchman can be questioned, however, he is shot and killed.
The young woman narrowly avoids the same fate.
A coatroom attendant shows up and states the agent checked his briefcase at the club where he works.
The detective and the inspector wait to see who will claim it.
It is the manservant, the executive's butler.
He claims that the executive left him a note instructing him to get the briefcase.
Upon close inspection, the detective concludes it is a forgery.
While waiting for the executive to return to his apartment, the son is entrusted to take vital fingerprint evidence to the authorities.
He is promptly mugged in the elevator and the evidence stolen.
Scolding is postponed when somebody finally turns on the lights in the executive's office and finds his dead body hidden behind his desk.
He had been killed by poisoned brandy, and apparently by somebody he trusted who he was having a friendly drink with.
The detective decides to gather all the suspects at the airport the next day.
The airplane, rigged the night before to release poison gas when it dives, takes off for a test flight with nearly everyone aboard.
As the bomber starts to descend, the classmate grabs the falling glass globe containing the gas.
When they land, he smashes the globe, gets out and locks the door.
However, the police are waiting to apprehend him, and the detective and the rest emerge unscathed (the trap had been found during an inspection and rendered harmless).
The classmate cannot be the ringleader, as the latter is known to be a younger man.
He refuses to identify his leader.
When the detective asks for a glass of water for the classmate, the stockbroker gets it for him, falling into the detective's trap.
The detective samples the water and identifies the same poison that was found in the executive's brandy.
